This is a petition filed u/s. 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, claiming for compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:

On 1-5-11 at about 4.30 p.m. when he was travelling as a passenger in an Auto bearing No.KA.42/6015 along with other passengers towards Harohalli, the driver of the Auto by driving the vehicle with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner without observing the traffic rules, near Medamaranahalli cross, he lost the control over the vehicle and made it to topple towards the road side.
Due to the impact of the said accident, the petitioner claims that he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and other passenger sustained simple injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Shubhodaya Clinic for first-aid-treatment and then he was shifted to Shubhash hospital, Bidadi for better treatment and then he was shifted to KIMS hospital, Bangalore and there he was treated as an inpatient.
The petitioner claims that he has become bed ridden and he spent Rs.40,000/- towards medical and other incidental expenses.
The petitioner claims that he was working as Contractor at BWSSB, Bangalore and was earning Rs.10,00,000/- p.a. prior to the accident.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he became disabled and not in a position to lead normal life.

The petitioner claims that the accident took place due to the negligence of the driver of the Auto and in this regard the jurisdictional Harohalli police registered the case against the driver of the Auto in Cr.109/11 and charge sheeted him for the cause of the accident.
Hence the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle and the respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence this petition.
3. Respondent Nos.1 & 2 appeared before the court through their counsels on receiving the notice and filed their written statement separately.
4. The respondent No.1 filed their written statement denying the averments of the petition as false.

The respondent No.1 denied the issuance of the policy in respect of the offending vehicle in para-3 of the written statement and claims that even if the policy is issued, their liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

The respondent No.1 further claims that the vehicle has been falsely implicated by the petitioner, by colluding with the jurisdictional police and with the 2 nd respondent and hence there is a delay of 15 days in lodging the complaint about the alleged accident.

sentences.text: On perusal of the records, as rightly argued by the counsel for the respondent there was a delay of 18 days in filing of the complaint as per Ex-P1 FIR has been registered on 19-5-2011 on the basis of the complaint filed by the petitioner on 19-5-2011.

Nevertheless, though there is a delay of 18 days in filing the complaint, but mere only on the basis of the delay, this court cannot come to the conclusion that the case of the petitioner is weak or unbelievable.
All other facts and circumstances and the reasons for the delay in filing the complaint has to be looked into.

On perusal of Ex-P2 complaint, petitioner has clearly stated that soon after the accident, he was taken to the hospital by the public and thereafter from the said hospital, he was shifted to KMC hospital, Bangalore for further treatment and hence there was a delay in filing the complaint as he was taking the treatment in the hospital.
Even PW-1 in his evidence and further evidence clearly stated that soon after the accident, he was shifted to the hospital and he was treated as inpatient from 5-5-2011 to 23-5-2011.

further PW-1 in his further additional evidence at para 3 clearly stated that he has given the request letter to the duty doctor and for giving the complaint with regard to the accident as other two passengers has not lodged complaint against the said auto and thereafter after taking permission from the hospital to go to home and lodge the complaint before police he has went to the police station on 19-5-2011 and given the complaint before the police station on 19-5-2011.

It is pertinent to note here that in the further cross-examination of the PW-1 on 12-3-2025 respondent counsel has not at all denied the reasons stated by the PW-1 in his additional affidavit as to the reasons for the delay.

Even it is not disputed by the respondent counsel about the injuries sustained by the PW-1 and the treatment taken by him with respect to the said injuries in the hospital from 1-5- 2011 till 23-5-2011.

17. Apart from this, on perusal of the wound certificate, Ex-P6, it is clear that petitioner was taken to the Subhash medical centre by the public soon after the accident at 6.45 p.m. with alleged history of toppling of the auto near Medanahalli at around 5.30.p.m.
Ex-P6 clearly shows that petitioner has been met with an accident due to the topling of the auto near Medanahalli on 1-5-2011 and he was shifted to the hospital soon after the accident.
Thus reasons stated by the PW-1 with regard to the delay in filing the complaint appears to be satisfactory and genuine.

18. In this regard, I would like to rely upon the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in - (2011) 4 SCC 693 Ravi V/s Bhadrinarayana, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that - " It is well settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian Conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after the accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of the kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay the Courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so, the contents of FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons, then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.

The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily Nagaraju M Y vs Bharati Aix General Insurance Co Ltd on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169546687/
5 to intimate the Police to initiate investigation of Criminal offences.

Thus in view of the above all said facts, it can be safely concluded that on 1-5-2011 petitioner along with other passengers was travelling in the offending vehicle and offending vehicle which was met with accident by toppling up side and down and due to which petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

27. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature,
the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
28. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Though the respondents have denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.

29. In addenda, in a claim for compensation U/Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

31. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 46 years.
The petitioner has produced the Ex-P.27-aadhaar card which reveals petitioner's date of birth is 10-1-1965 and as on the date of accident, he was 46 years.

The petitioner has stated that he was working as Contractor at BWSSB,
Bangalore and earning Rs.10,00,000/- per annum and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and deformity.

It was contended by the petitioner that he was a contractor at BWSSB and was earning Rs.10 lakhs p.a. and after the said accident he was unable to lead normal life as earlier and not able to do his job as earlier and suffering from huge loss of income.

In support of his contention, petitioner has produced his pan card, registration certificate as per Ex-P10 and VAT registration certificate as per Ex-P11 and certificate of tax deduction as per Ex- P12 and 13.
Ex-P10 document shows that petitioner was a registered contractor in BWSSB for a block period of 2008-2010.
Further as per Ex-P12 and 13, it was a certificate of tax deduction issued by the Executive Engineer, BWSSB which shows that petitioner was paying the tax in respect of his works.
Further Ex-P14 and 15 form No.16 for the year 2007-2008 and 2010- 2011
shows that tax has been deducted from the payments received by the petitioner.
According to Ex- P14 and 15, petitioner has paid Rs.13,663/- in the year 2008 and Rs.14,216/- in the year 2011 towards the tax on the payments received by him.

Though the documents produced by the petitioner proves that petitioner was working as a contractor in BWSSB, but Ex-P14 and 15 only shows about the deduction of the tax on the payment received by the petitioner, it does not disclose what was the actual income of the petitioner.

We cannot consider all the payments received by the petitioner shown in Ex-P14 and 15 as his income as those payments were received by the petitioner as a contractor towards his contract work done by him.

Admittedly petitioner has invested on men and materials for doing the contract work and the payment made to him includes investment made by him and the expenses incurred by him towards the men and materials.
Hence all those payments received by the petitioner cannot be considered as a income of the petitioner.
Petitioner has not clearly stated not produced any documents to show that what is his actual income after the deduction of his expenses.
Hence notional income of the petitioner is taken into consideration.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
if his income is assessed at Rs.6,500/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.

his health condition was stable and fracture has been united.

34. Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
With regard to the disability in RTA cases, the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar -vs- Ajay Kumar and Another.
35. Now it is to be seen whether the disability assessed by the doctor impairs the avocation of the petitioner.
There is nothing on record to believe that the petitioner's contract licence has been cancelled due to the accidental injuries or he has not doing any Contractor work.

36. At this stage it is worth to refer here the unreported judgment in MFA No.2973/2005 North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation Vs. Somappa Rudrappa Kuravinkoppa decided on 19072005 wherein it was observed by the Hon'ble High Court that "in case of clavicle and mandible fracture there would be no consequences loss of future earning capacity.

entities.text: MFA No.2973/2005 North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation Vs. Somappa Rudrappa Kuravinkoppa
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, any compensation under the said head is impermissible.
37. In this case the PW.2 has assessed the disability of permanent physical impairment of 16%.

By considering the judgment above referred the petitioner has sustained acromic clavicular joint fracture with dislocation and from the said injury no permanent disability would be caused so as to assess the future loss of income.
Hence, this court declines to grant any compensation under the head loss of future income.
38. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained acromic clavicular joint fracture with dislocation and pain and swelling over right shoulder, on that day he was treated conservatively with POP and advised to use arm pouch and discharged on 2-5-2011 and doctor opined that the said injury is grievous in nature.

sentences.text: The petitioner has stated that he is suffering with permanent disablement and deformity to attend his work and to do daily activities.
Hence petitioner is suffering from whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 46 years, certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.

40. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by him and duration of his stay in the KIMS hospital & Research Centre, Bangalore from 1-5-2021 to 2-5-2021 and 5-5-2011 to 23-5-2011 for 21 days as inpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 3 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.19,500/- (6,500 X 3) under the head loss of income during the laid-up period.
41.

ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is a resident of New Guddadahalli,
Mysore road, Bangalore and has taken treatment as inpatient at KIMS hospital & Research Centre,
Bangalore from 1-5-2021 to 5-5-2021 and from 5-5-2011 to 23-5-2011 for 21 days as inpatient and certainly he would have hired the cab for traveling to the hospital and treated conservatively with POP and advised to use arm pouch and discharged on 2-5-2011.

Further petitioner was admitted as inpatient at KIMS hospital on 5-5-2011 for further management and on 9- 5-2011 ORIF with hook plate with ligament reconstruction done, manipulation of screw with K wire fixation done on 13-5-2011 and discharged on 23-5-2011 and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of his treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.
Hence a sum of Rs.15,000/- under this head.
42. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:

The petitioner being the owner cum driver by profession, certainly injuries sustained by him will cause discomfort and some disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.

Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment &
frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded under this head.
43. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced Ex-P18-four advance receipts for Rs.19,500/-, Ex-P19 medical bills for Rs.36,106/- and Ex-P20 prescriptions.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.55,606/- under the head of medical expenses.

45. INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Respondent No.1 has taken the contention that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having the valid driving licence and valid permit.
On the other hand, the owner of the vehicle RW-1 has produced the insurance copy as per Ex-R1 which shows that he has obtained the commercial policy from the respondent No.1 Bharathi AXI.

even produced the paid receipt which shows that as on the date of accident, the offending vehicle was duly insured with the respondent No.1.

Further RW-1 has produced the permit in respect of particular contract of carriage as per Ex-R3 which shows that there was a permit from 2010 to 2015 to carry the passengers 3 + 1.
Ex-R4 is the letter issued by the respondent No.1 to the respondent No.2.
Ex-R5 is also the permit extract.

Thus Ex-R1, Ex-R2 and Ex-R3 clearly establish that the driver of the offending vehicle was having valid DL and permit and vehicle was duly insured with the respondent No.1 as on the date of accident and respondent No.2 has not committed breach of any of the conditions of the policy.
46. Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
47. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.1 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On perusal of Ex-P2 complaint, petitioner has clearly stated that soon after the accident, he was taken to the hospital by the public and thereafter from the said hospital, he was shifted to KMC hospital, Bangalore for further treatment and hence there was a delay in filing the complaint as he was taking the treatment in the hospital.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay the Courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so, the contents of FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.
If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons, then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily Nagaraju M Y vs Bharati Aix General Insurance Co Ltd on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169546687/
5 to intimate the Police to initiate investigation of Criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves the factum of accident, so that victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay is doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.
From the facts of the complaint and from the evidence of the PW-1 and looking into the damages caused to the auto as seen from Ex-P5 seizure mahazar and also fact that the auto itself has toppled upside down and no other vehicle involved in the accident itself establish that on that day driver of the auto was driving in high speed, rash and negligent manner, due to which he lost control over the vehicle and made the auto to turn upside down and thereby caused the accident.
24. Even the respondent has not brought any materials and evidence on record to prove that charge filed against the driver of the auto is defective or collusive.
Even in the present case, there is no materials and evidence placed on record to prove that the charge sheet and the police documents are collusive and effective.
26. Thus in view of the above all said facts, it can be safely concluded that on 1-5-2011 petitioner along with other passengers was travelling in the offending vehicle and offending vehicle which was met with accident by toppling up side and down and due to which petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Though the respondents have denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.
29. In addenda, in a claim for compensation U/Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.
Admittedly petitioner has invested on men and materials for doing the contract work and the payment made to him includes investment made by him and the expenses incurred by him towards the men and materials.
Hence all those payments received by the petitioner cannot be considered as a income of the petitioner.
Petitioner has not clearly stated not produced any documents to show that what is his actual income after the deduction of his expenses.
Hence notional income of the petitioner is taken into consideration.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
if his income is assessed at Rs.6,500/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
